name: availability-calendar
title: Availability calendar
description: A read-only calendar of free, booked and on-request days for rentals, venues and rooms, told apart by pattern and a legend in words, never by colour.
docs: booked and onRequest are lists of days ('2026-03-14') and runs ({ start, end }, both included): a day is a day on the calendar, so nothing shifts with a time zone, and a booked day wins over a day on request. Every day is a grid cell named in full ('Friday 14 March, available', '..., booked', '..., on request', '..., past'), with a pattern of its own: blank for free, a diagonal hatch for booked, dots and a dashed edge for on request. The legend names them in words, and minStay writes 'Minimum stay: 3 nights' beside it. On a hatched or dotted day the number sits on a small chip, so the pattern never runs through it. The grid is a keyboard grid with one tab stop: arrow keys move by day and week, Home and End to the ends of the week, Page Up and Page Down by month (Shift for a year), and the view follows. months is 1 or 2: two months sit side by side, each with its own title and an arrow at the outer edge, once the calendar itself is 36rem wide (a container query), and stack with one toolbar above them when it is narrower. today ('2026-03-09') mutes the days before it and puts a dot under it; leave it out to use the browser's clock in timeZone, read once the page is live: until then, and unless defaultMonth or month names the month, the calendar only holds its place at a fixed height and the grid appears once the page is live, so a page that is built ahead of time (static, cached) should pass defaultMonth. month and onMonthChange control the first month shown, or defaultMonth sets it. locale writes the month and day names, weekStartsOn is 1 (Monday) or 0, and labels carries every word. It only displays: pair it with the date range picker when people must choose dates.
